input.reflection:
Second consecutive disciplined no-trade day. The decision was overdetermined: (1) already at 7 open positions vs my own 5-position cap, so the risk manager would reject any new entry regardless of merit; (2) the top two Super candidates STX and LITE are both literally at 0.0% from 52w high, well past their VCP pivots — the textbook 'extended-from-pivot' trap that my rule [744aa229] flags as statistically negative EV (43% vs 54% baseline, p=0.037); (3) no catalyst worth chasing.

What's encouraging: the book is doing the work. Earnings sweep is clean for 7+ days across all 7 holdings — the 4/29 process rule has become reflexive. Winners are running (MU +24.4%, FIX +12.4%, VRT +11.3%, AMAT +7.8%), only GEV slightly red at -0.4% which is well within tolerance in a strong tape (QQQ +1.3%). No book actions required.

Reinforced lesson from yesterday: when the top Super names are extended (STX two days running at 0.0% from high), the screener is showing me late-stage strength, not entry points. The intersection of 'strong stock' and 'low-risk entry' is small most days. The shadow log over-trading bias (14 would-buys / 1 skip in 5 days) is a real warning — I need the live discipline to match the codified rules. Today's inaction is the correct trade.

No new rule warranted — today's situation is fully covered by existing rules (5-position cap, far-from-pivot avoidance, earnings sweep). Execution > new theory.
